title: Solving Systems by Graphing
short: Graph both lines and read the intersection.
trouble: Students report only the x-coordinate as the solution.

blocks.html: Since the solution of a system is where the lines cross, one way to find it is to draw both lines carefully, using what you know about slope and intercept.

Graphing shows every solution of each equation at once, so the crossing point can be seen. A drawing is only as exact as the grid, though: if the crossing lands between grid lines, you can only estimate it. That is why you always check the point in both equations.
To solve by graphing: graph both lines, find where they intersect, write the point as $(x, y)$, and check it in both equations.

blocks.title: Read the crossing
steps: First line: start at $(0, 1)$, then up 1 and right 1 each step.
Second line: start at $(0, 7)$, then down 2 and right 1 each step.

blocks.title: A fractional slope
steps: First line: from $(0, 3)$, up 1 for every 2 to the right (or down 1 for every 2 to the left).
Second line: through the origin, down 1 for every 1 to the right.

blocks.html: Reporting only the $x$-coordinate, as in “the solution is $x = 2$.” A system in $x$ and $y$ needs both values: the solution is the point $(2, 3)$.
